chunk_findings.detail: `test_the_mcp_view_family_action_gives_the_same_plan` calls `Server(repo)` with positional arguments that do not match the expected `Server` class signature in `ddflow.surfaces.mcp`, raising a `TypeError` during test execution and causing the test suite to fail on this test.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_spawn_plan.py:270

chunk_findings.detail: In `_route`, `got` is `None` both when the endpoint has no `api_key_env` and when `E.resolve_key` cannot resolve a required key. The expression `bool(got) if got is not None else True` therefore reports “key present” for a missing required key whenever `E.resolve_key` returns `None` (the usual optional-key lookup result). For a route whose endpoint declares `api_key_env=OPENAI_API_KEY` but the environment variable is unset, `ddflow spawn --plan --worker claude --route that-route` will set `route.has_key: true` and omit the `missing key` refusal, returning an instruct snippet that assumes the key is available. That contradicts the stated acceptance that missing key names must be refused.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/spawn.py:57

chunk_findings.detail: `_from_descriptor` fetches the table entry and comments that it “still supplies what the descriptor lacks”, but it only merges `binary` and `native` from the table. It drops table-supplied `model_format`, `effort_values`, `budget_flag`, `cwd_flag`, `permissions`, `permission_notes`, and `unverified`. Given a harness that has a headless descriptor and a `spawn_facts.toml` entry using the same schema `_from_table` accepts, e.g. `budget_flag = "--max-budget-usd"`, `permissions = {yolo = ["--yolo"]}`, and `effort_values = ["low", "high"]`, `load` returns `budget_flag=""`, `permissions={}`, `effort_values=()`, and a hardcoded “no budget flag” unverified reason. A plan for `--budget-usd 2 --permissions yolo --effort medium` then omits the known budget and permission flags (or refuses them) and may pass an arbitrary effort value, even though the table knew the correct facts.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/spawn/facts.py:105-119 (`_from_descriptor`)

chunk_findings.detail: The native route unconditionally sets `"model": model` in the constructed `args` dict, overwriting any default model the descriptor placed in `f.native.arguments`. The process route correctly guards this with `if model and f.model_flag`, but the native path has no equivalent guard. Concrete scenario: a descriptor for `claude` carries `native.arguments = {"model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514", "subagent_type": "code"}`. The operator runs `ddflow spawn --plan --worker claude --master claude` with no `--model` and `spawn.require_model = false`. `_consider` marks native as usable (no asked items). In `_route_body`, `model` is `""` (from `spec.model`), so the spread `**f.native.arguments` puts `"model": "claude-sonnet-4-20250514"` into `args`, then the next line overwrites it with `"model": ""`. The emitted `native_call` tells the master's harness to invoke the tool with an empty model string instead of the descriptor's default, which either errors or selects an unintended model. The fix mirrors the process route: only include `"model"` in `args` when `model` is non-empty.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/spawn/plan.py `_route_body` (native branch)

chunk_findings.detail: `render.text` formats `budget_ceiling_usd` with the `:g` spec but does not handle a missing/unknown ceiling. The same line already treats `budget_usd is None` as `"none"`, so a plan with no budget cap (for example `--budget-usd 2` when no ceiling is configured, or simply no cap) can have `caps["budget_ceiling_usd"] is None`; then the f-string raises `TypeError: unsupported format string passed to NoneType.__format__` instead of printing that there is no ceiling or listing it as unverified.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/spawn/render.py (caps line in `text`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_call` forwards the caller’s `plan` flag verbatim (`plan=bool(a.get("plan"))`), while the `plan` parameter declared at line 64 is optional and has no `default=True` or `required=True`. Therefore an invocation such as `ddflow spawn --worker kilo --master auto` (or the MCP `spawn` action without `plan`) calls `ddflow.api.spawn.spawn(..., plan=False)`. The command’s contract says it is “read-only by construction” and “starts nothing,” and the help says plan is “the only mode,” but this surface does not enforce that: it can hand a non-plan request to the API. If the API’s `plan=False` branch is the spawn/execute path (as the parameter name implies), this defeats the “zero launch risk” intent; if the API rejects `plan=False`, the command is still wrong because its advertised summary promises a plan without requiring `--plan`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/declared/spawn.py:19 (`_call`)

chunk_findings.detail: The help tells MCP users to call `ddflow_view action=spawn plan=true ...`, but the accepted surface for this change is the existing `ddflow_lanes` tool with `view=spawn` (no new top-level tool). An agent that follows the help will call the wrong MCP tool/action; if the surface is `ddflow_lanes`, the call fails or bypasses the intended lanes view, and if the code really exposes `ddflow_view`, the documented surface still violates the accepted MCP surface contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/spawn.md:35

chunk_findings.detail: The documented response contract says `mode=spawn` when local and `launch` holds the spec, while `instruct`/`agent_action` appears only when the caller is an agent or `--remote` is used. The accepted plan must always include `local` and an `instruct` snippet for the master's harness, even for a local spawn. For input `--master claude --worker kilo --model m` where the binary is present, a consumer following this help would look for `launch` and not the required `instruct` snippet (or `local` field), so the plan is unusable for the specified contract.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/prompts/help/spawn.md:24

chunk_findings.detail: The `[harness.claude.native]` table declares `subagent_type` as unverified (`unverified_args = ["subagent_type"]`) but the immediately following `[harness.claude.native.arguments]` table fills it with `subagent_type = "general-purpose"` (line 46). Given a native plan where the master and worker are both `claude` and no effort/permissions/budget is requested, the generated Agent call will contain the unverified `subagent_type: general-purpose` fact, violating the stated contract that unknown/unverified facts are listed as unverified and never filled. If the loader instead strips `unverified_args`, the same plan omits the `subagent_type` argument that the acceptance criteria say the Claude Agent call must include.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/spawn_facts.toml:44

chunk_findings.detail: The docs tell MCP callers to use `ddflow_view action=spawn` and give the example `ddflow_view action=spawn plan=true worker=kilo model=provider/model item=X1`, but the stated intent requires the action to be on the existing `ddflow_lanes` tool (`view=spawn`) and explicitly says no new top-level tool. An agent or operator following this docs will call the wrong MCP tool and fail to obtain the spawn plan.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/spawn-plan.md:26

chunk_findings.detail: The docs describe the plan as exposing `mode` with values `spawn` and `instruct`, and say only `instruct` mode contains `agent_action`. The acceptance says the plan must always return `local` and `instruct`, where `instruct` is the exact snippet for the master's harness. For a local caller such as `ddflow spawn --plan --master claude --worker kilo`, this docs implies the result would have `mode=spawn` and only `launch`, omitting the required `instruct` snippet.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/spawn-plan.md:21

chunk_findings.detail: The `no_worker_starts` fixture does not actually enforce the “run nothing” property it is used to prove. It only patches `subprocess.Popen` and only rejects calls whose first argument’s basename is exactly one of `WORKERS`. A worker can still be started through the same patched `Popen` with `shell=True` or through a shell wrapper, e.g. `subprocess.Popen("kilo run --model m ...", shell=True)` or `subprocess.Popen(["/bin/sh", "-c", "kilo run --model m ..."])`; `os.path.basename` yields the full shell string or `sh`, which is not in `WORKERS`, so the guard passes while `kilo` is launched. Since `test_planning_starts_no_worker_process` relies on this fixture, it can pass even when planning starts a worker, and the other direct `P.plan` tests do not use the guard at all.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_spawn_plan.py:no_worker_starts

chunk_findings.detail: `binary` is resolved only when the first argv token is `{binary}`. If a descriptor’s headless argv uses the binary placeholder after a literal wrapper, e.g. `headless.argv = ["env", "{binary}", "{brief}"]`, `_from_descriptor` sets `binary="env"` because `argv[0] != BINARY`, ignoring any table binary and leaving `{binary}` in the argv template. A plan that substitutes `Facts.binary` into `{binary}` or uses `Facts.binary` to decide local availability will then run/check the wrapper (`env`) instead of the actual worker binary; with a table entry `binary="worker"` it still reports `env`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/spawn/facts.py:_from_descriptor

chunk_findings.detail: `_flag_checks` returns early when `inp.facts is None` before the budget-ceiling and budget-enforcement checks at lines 249 and 257. Given `Inputs(facts=None, worker_known=True, budget_ceiling=10.0, spawn=SpawnConfig(require_model=False, require_budget_cap=True, route_order=("manual",), max_children=1, max_depth=1, default_profile=""))` and `Spec(worker="kilo", budget_usd=100.0, worktree="none")`, `_checks` produces no refusal, `plan` then chooses `manual` and returns `ready=True`; `p.caps` shows `budget_usd=100.0` and `budget_ceiling_usd=10.0` even though the documented cap should have produced `budget_over_ceiling`. The same early return also bypasses `require_budget_cap`, effort, and permission checks when facts are absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/spawn/plan.py:_flag_checks:229

chunk_findings.detail: When the invalid permissions profile comes from the config default and the worker has no permissions profiles, the suggested “next” call cannot fix the refusal. Given `facts.permissions={}`, `spawn.default_profile="bad"`, and `spec.permissions=""`, `_flag_checks` refuses `permissions_unknown` and calls `_again(spec, permissions="")`. `_again` omits empty values at line 147, so the suggested command is the same `ddflow spawn --plan --worker <harness>` without `--permissions`; re-running it still resolves `profile="bad"` from the default knob and refuses identically. The refusal therefore does not name a call that can succeed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/spawn/plan.py:_flag_checks:247

chunk_findings.detail: The record uses `spec.model`, not the model actually resolved by the plan. Given `Spec(worker="kilo", model="")` and `Inputs(route=RouteInfo(id="fast", model_arg="new-model"))`, `plan` resolves `model="new-model"` and `_argv` passes that value to the worker’s model flag, but `_record` writes `model=-` in the note text (or `model=old-model` if `spec.model` and the route model differ). The resulting `agent_action.record` and CLI note misreport the effective model, which is wrong for cost/audit records.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/spawn/plan.py:_record:330

chunk_findings.detail: When `remote=True`, a route with a required key that is not resolved on the ddflow machine is neither refused nor listed as unverified. Given `Inputs(remote=True, route=RouteInfo(id="x", model_arg="m", key_env="FOO", key_ok=False), facts=<usable process facts>)`, `_route_checks` skips the `key_unset` refusal because of `not inp.remote`, and `_unverified` only adds the binary-installed unknown at line 379. The plan returns ready with a process argv that uses the route model, but the caller gets no warning that `$FOO` may be missing, contrary to “unknown facts are listed unverified, never filled.”

chunk_findings.detail: The `manual_brief` branch emits only the label “give the worker this brief:” and never emits the manual brief itself. For a plan such as `{"worker": "kilo", "master": "claude", "route": "manual", "mode": "manual", "refused": [], "instruct": {"manual_brief": "run ddflow dispatch claim ... then run kilo ..."}, "agent_action": None, "claim": None, "record": None, "launch": None, "run": {"reason": "manual"}, "caps": {...}, "identity": {"agent": "x"}, "notes": [], "unverified": [], "brief": ""}`, `render.text()` returns the label but omits the required snippet. The intent requires the text plan to include the exact printed manual brief for a manual route; here the caller gets an empty instruction block (or only the later lane brief if `plan["brief"]` happens to be non-empty).

chunk_findings.detail: The command is declared as a plan-only, read-only surface, but `_call` forwards `plan=bool(a.get("plan"))` and the `plan` parameter is optional with no default. An MCP call such as `{"worker": "kilo"}` (valid because only `worker` is required) or an explicit `{"plan": false, "worker": "kilo"}` therefore invokes `ddflow.api.spawn.spawn(..., plan=False)`. This accepts a non-plan mode that the command’s own help describes as invalid (“Plan only (the only mode: no worker is started)”). If the API’s `plan=False` branch implements the spawn/run path implied by the verb and the phrase “Plan (plan=true)”, a surface documented as starting nothing can attempt to start a worker; even if it does not, invalid input is silently passed instead of being rejected.

chunk_findings.detail: The help tells MCP callers to use `ddflow_view action=spawn`, but the change’s acceptance specifies that the read-only spawn action is exposed on the existing `ddflow_lanes` tool (with the action/view shape noted as `view=spawn`) and explicitly says there is no new top-level MCP tool. An operator following the help issues a `ddflow_view` MCP call; if the implementation follows the specified `ddflow_lanes` action, that call fails as an unknown tool/action, so the plan cannot be retrieved over MCP. If the code instead exposes `ddflow_view`, the help documents a top-level tool contrary to the stated MCP budget.

chunk_findings.detail: The Claude native fallback declares `subagent_type` as unverified (`unverified_args = ["subagent_type"]`) at line 45, yet immediately supplies a concrete value for it at line 47 (`subagent_type = "general-purpose"`). The ACCEPT says unknown facts are listed unverified and never filled. Given `ddflow spawn --plan --master claude --worker claude`, a plan built from this fallback table can emit a native Agent instruction containing `subagent_type: general-purpose` as a fact even though the same table marks that argument unverified; if the Claude Agent tool rejects that key or value, the operator is given an invalid spawn snippet.

chunk_findings.detail: The documentation tells MCP callers to invoke `ddflow_view action=spawn ...`, while the stated interface for this change is a `spawn` view on the existing `ddflow_lanes` tool (`view=spawn`) and explicitly says no new top-level MCP tool should be added. An agent following this page calls the wrong tool/parameter, so the documented `ddflow_view action=spawn plan=true ...` invocation will fail to return the plan (or the implementation introduces a new top-level MCP action contrary to the stated MCP budget).
